dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 马克，你今天想吃什么？

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我叫马克，我非常喜欢运动。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 因为我天天运动，所以身体很好。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我姐姐问我：“你怎么天天吃这么多？”

dialogue.english: My sister asked me, "How come you eat so much every day?"

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 好吧，那就明天开始少吃一点儿吧！
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo ba, nà jiù míngtiān kāishǐ shǎo chī yìdiǎnr ba!
dialogue.english: All right — tomorrow I'll start eating a bit less!

explanation.hanzi: 在HSK 1里，“怎么 + 动词”问方法，比如“这个字怎么读？”。“怎么”也可以问原因，意思和“为什么”差不多，可是常常表示说话人觉得奇怪、没想到。“怎么”放在主语后面、动词或形容词前面，比如“你怎么不吃了？”。
explanation.english: You already know 怎么 + verb asking HOW to do something (这个字怎么读?). 怎么 can also ask WHY — like 为什么, but with a note of surprise: "How come …?" The speaker has noticed something unexpected. It goes after the subject and before the verb or adjective, and often comes with 不 / 没 / 还 / 这么: 你怎么不吃了? (How come you've stopped eating?), 他怎么还没来? (Why isn't he here yet?). Use 为什么 for a neutral question about reasons; use 怎么 when you're surprised.

How come he's not here yet?
Why is it so cold today?

title.english: Reduplicated Measure Words: "Every" (天天, 个个)

explanation.hanzi: 有的量词和名词可以说两次，表示“每一……”，比如“天天”就是“每天”，“个个”就是“每个”，“件件”就是“每件”。后面常常有“都”。
explanation.english: Say certain measure words (or time words) twice and they mean "every one, without exception": 天天 = 每天 "every day", 个个 = 每个 "every one", 件件 = 每件 "every piece", 人人 "everyone", 年年 "every year". The doubled word usually comes before the verb and is followed by 都. It sounds a little livelier than 每…… . Note: it can't be followed by a noun — say 个个都很大, not 个个苹果.

examples.pinyin: Mǎkè tiāntiān dōu qù dǎ lánqiú.
examples.english: Mark goes to play basketball every day.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē píngguǒ gège dōu hěn dà.
examples.english: Every one of these apples is big.

examples.hanzi: 她的衣服件件都很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yīfu jiànjiàn dōu hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Every one of her clothes is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 这儿的羊肉面条人人都说好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhèr de yángròu miàntiáo rénrén dōu shuō hǎochī.
examples.english: Everyone says the lamb noodles here are delicious.

rows: 我的同学个个都会说汉语。

explanation.hanzi: “因为”说原因，“所以”说结果。原因在前面，结果在后面。“因为”和“所以”可以一起用，也可以只用一个。
explanation.english: 因为 introduces the cause and 所以 introduces the result. In Chinese the cause normally comes first and the result second. Unlike English, it's perfectly natural to use both words in the same sentence (因为……，所以……). You can also drop one of them: 因为下雨了，我们不去了 / 下雨了，所以我们不去了. When the reason comes second, use only 因为: 我今天没去学校，因为我生病了.

examples.hanzi: 因为下雨了，所以我们不去打篮球了。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ le, suǒyǐ wǒmen bú qù dǎ lánqiú le.
examples.english: It's raining, so we're not going to play basketball.

examples.hanzi: 因为他经常游泳，所以身体很好。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā jīngcháng yóu yǒng, suǒyǐ shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He swims a lot, so he's very fit.

examples.hanzi: 因为这个饭店的鱼很好吃，所以人很多。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi zhège fàndiàn de yú hěn hǎochī, suǒyǐ rén hěn duō.
examples.english: The fish at this restaurant is delicious, so it's always busy.

examples.hanzi: 我今天没去学校，因为我生病了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méi qù xuéxiào, yīnwèi wǒ shēng bìng le.
examples.english: I didn't go to school today because I was ill.

singleComponentChars.etymology: The traditional form 門 is a clear picture of a double door with two swinging leaves. The simplified form keeps the outline: a dot for the top of the left leaf and a frame with a hook for the right.
A front view of a sheep's head: the two dots at the top are curling horns, the horizontal lines are the face and ears, and the long vertical stroke runs down the middle of the head.

radicals.english: heart radical at the bottom (thoughts and feelings)

prompt.hanzi: 小组活动：问问同学喜欢吃什么、经常做什么运动，然后说说为什么。
prompt.english: Group activity: find out what your classmates like to eat and what sport they do — and why.

activities: Survey: ask three classmates 你经常做什么运动？ 一个星期几天？ and 你最喜欢吃什么？ Report back with 因为……，所以…… .
Surprise questions: one person mimes something unexpected (not eating, yawning, carrying a basketball). The others ask 你怎么……？ and the mimer answers with 因为…… .
Every-day habits: take turns saying one thing you do 天天 and one thing your family members 个个都…… (e.g. 我的家人个个都喜欢吃面条).
